headline: High: Haystack’s broad egress/MCP plus Unstructured’s filesystem and subprocess access create default pathways for leakage, prompt injection, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so it may ingest external content or tool outputs; Unstructured reads documents and can write files, creating a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled document text reaches Haystack as instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Unstructured outputs attacker-controlled document text into a shared workspace that Haystack later parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF Haystack is configured to consume MCP or REST content without provenance filtering, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict Haystack to trusted MCP endpoints only.
Add provenance tags to all Unstructured outputs before Haystack reads them.
Disable automatic instruction-following on parsed document text.
Review one sample document-to-prompt path end-to-end.
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents into separate workspaces with explicit handoff files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call APIs, while Unstructured reads and writes documents and touches text/images. If sensitive documents are processed by Unstructured and then forwarded through Haystack, data can leave the local boundary in default-like workflows. The profiles do not prove shared storage, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same document workspace, Haystack can transmit document-derived content off-host.
IF Unstructured processes sensitive documents and Haystack sends retrieved snippets to external APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Limit Haystack egress to approved destinations only.
Keep sensitive documents out of shared directories.
Turn on redaction before any handoff from Unstructured to Haystack.
Audit one representative document flow for outbound requests.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Unstructured can read/write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress. That overlap creates a realistic conflict on shared mutable resources or shared orchestration state, especially if both touch the same workspace. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF Haystack and Unstructured share an orchestrator without locks, concurrent mutations can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Disable package installation unless needed.
Check for concurrent runs before starting a second instance.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can surface retrieved facts, and Unstructured turns documents into text that Haystack may consume. That makes a plausible chain where Unstructured’s extraction errors become authoritative inputs for Haystack outputs. Because no verification step is documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Haystack uses Unstructured output as retrieval ground truth, extraction mistakes can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts Haystack outputs without human review, the error blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add a verification step before Haystack acts on extracted text.
Sample-check one extracted document for fidelity.
Mark Unstructured output as untrusted metadata.
Require human approval for downstream actions.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and source-link preservation.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack’s documented data class is anonymous usage statistics, while Unstructured touches documents, images, and text. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but Unstructured exposes a privacy-policy endpoint and Haystack has broad egress, so a compliance gap is possible if regulated documents are routed through them. Only Unstructured is cited because the issue is primarily its document handling; Haystack is cited for egress context.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by Unstructured and then sent through Haystack, policy review is required.
IF the deployment requires strict residency or retention guarantees, the current profiles do not demonstrate them.
mitigations: Confirm both vendors’ retention settings.
Avoid routing regulated documents through the pair.
Review the privacy-policy and docs endpoints once.
Log which document classes are processed.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement controls.
